name: Clique-width
description: A graph parameter equal to the minimum number of labels needed to construct a graph using vertex creation, disjoint union, relabeling, and adding all edges between two label classes.

name: Hereditary graph class
description: A class of graphs closed under taking induced subgraphs, equivalently definable by a (possibly infinite) family of forbidden induced subgraphs.

name: Boundedness of clique-width for H-free graphs
description: For each fixed graph H, the class of H-free graphs either has bounded clique-width or unbounded clique-width, and the boundary between these cases is characterized.

name: Cut distance and left convergence
description: A method that metrizes the space of graphs and graphons via the cut metric so that a sequence of dense graphs converges in homomorphism densities to a limit graphon.

name: Flag algebra method
description: Razborov's formalism that encodes asymptotic subgraph densities as elements of an algebra of partially labeled flags, reducing extremal inequalities to positive semidefinite combinations verifiable by SDP.

name: Topological connectedness of the independence complex
description: The topological connectivity of the simplicial complex whose faces are the independent sets of a graph, a homotopy-theoretic invariant of the graph.

name: Aharoni–Haxell topological Hall theorem
description: A system of sets has a system of disjoint representatives whenever, for every subfamily, the topological connectivity of the independence complex of the union exceeds the subfamily size minus two, a topological generalization of Hall's marriage theorem.

name: Independent transversal
description: Given a graph whose vertex set is partitioned into blocks, an independent set containing exactly one vertex from each block.

name: Long paths and cycles in expanders
description: Every expander graph with sufficiently good vertex- or spectral-expansion contains a path and a cycle whose length is linear in the number of vertices.

name: Supersingular isogeny graph
description: The Pizer/Ramanujan graph whose vertices are supersingular elliptic curves over a finite field of characteristic p and whose edges are ℓ-isogenies between them.

name: Isogeny-graph hardness / SIDH
description: The computational assumption that finding an isogeny path between two given supersingular elliptic curves in the isogeny graph is hard, underlying supersingular-isogeny Diffie–Hellman key exchange.

name: Delta-matroid
description: A set system (E, F) of feasible subsets satisfying a symmetric-exchange axiom, generalizing matroids by allowing feasible sets of differing cardinality.

name: Ribbon graph / embedded graph correspondence
description: The correspondence assigning to each ribbon graph a delta-matroid whose feasible sets are the spanning quasi-trees, generalizing the cycle matroid of a graph.

name: Ordered Ramsey/Turán theory
description: The study of extremal and Ramsey-type problems for graphs with a fixed linear order on the vertices, where forbidden patterns are ordered subgraphs.

name: Füredi–Hajnal theorem and interval chromatic number
description: The ordered Turán number of an ordered graph H is governed by its interval chromatic number, with ex<(n,H)=n^{2(1−1/χ<(H))+o(1)}.

name: Spherical building
description: A simplicial complex equipped with a system of apartments isomorphic to a finite Coxeter complex, axiomatizing the incidence geometry of a semisimple algebraic group of finite type.

name: Combinatorial construction of buildings
description: A method that builds a building from a chamber system or a group with a BN-pair by gluing apartments according to the Weyl group.

name: Stanley–Reisner ring
description: The quotient of a polynomial ring by the squarefree monomial ideal generated by the non-faces of a simplicial complex, encoding the complex's combinatorics in commutative-algebraic data.

name: Shellable complexes are Cohen–Macaulay
description: Every shellable simplicial complex has a Cohen–Macaulay Stanley–Reisner ring, linking the combinatorial shelling order to the algebraic Cohen–Macaulay property.

name: Hasse–Weil bound
description: The number N of points of a smooth projective curve of genus g over the field 𝔽_q satisfies |N − (q+1)| ≤ 2g√q.

name: Planar and exceptional polynomial functions
description: Polynomials over a finite field that are exceptional (define permutation maps over infinitely many extensions) or planar (whose difference maps are bijective), used in finite geometry and difference-set constructions.

name: Graph edge decomposition
description: A partition of the edge set of a graph into edge-disjoint subgraphs, each isomorphic to or drawn from a prescribed family.

name: Nash-Williams arboricity theorem
description: The minimum number of forests into which the edges of a graph can be partitioned equals the maximum over subgraphs H of ⌈|E(H)|/(|V(H)|−1)⌉.

name: Linear and star arboricity conjectures
description: Conjectured tight bounds on the minimum number of linear forests or star forests needed to decompose the edges of a d-regular graph, namely roughly ⌈(d+1)/2⌉ for linear arboricity.

name: Switching method
function_signature: (Class of combinatorial objects) → (Asymptotic enumeration / property estimate)
description: A counting technique that estimates the relative sizes of two classes of structures by bounding the number of local edge-switching operations between them.

name: Graph isomorphism problem
description: The computational decision problem of determining whether two given finite graphs are isomorphic.

name: Babai's quasipolynomial graph isomorphism algorithm
description: Graph isomorphism can be decided in quasipolynomial time exp((log n)^{O(1)}).

name: Weisfeiler–Leman algorithm and dimension
description: An iterative color-refinement procedure on k-tuples of vertices whose stable coloring is an isomorphism invariant; the WL dimension is the least k for which a graph is identified.

name: Graph and hypergraph decomposition (extremal)
description: The extremal problem of partitioning the edges of a (hyper)graph into copies of a fixed subgraph subject to divisibility and density conditions.

name: Existence of designs (Keevash; Glock–Kühn–Lo–Osthus)
description: For all admissible parameters and sufficiently large n satisfying the divisibility conditions, combinatorial designs (Steiner systems and more generally F-designs) exist, resolving the Existence Conjecture.

name: Absorption method
description: A technique that reserves a flexible absorbing substructure in advance so that any small leftover set produced by a near-perfect cover can be absorbed to complete a spanning configuration.

name: Iterative absorption
description: A refinement of the absorption method that repeatedly absorbs leftovers across a nested sequence of vortices, used to prove exact decomposition and spanning results in dense (hyper)graphs.

name: Borel combinatorics of graphs
description: The study of combinatorial structures on Borel graphs defined on standard Borel or measure spaces, requiring the solutions to be Borel or measurable.

name: Borel/measurable chromatic number
description: The least number of colors needed to properly color a Borel graph with the color classes required to be Borel or measurable sets.

name: Johnson graph
description: The graph J(n,k) whose vertices are the k-subsets of an n-set, with two subsets adjacent when their intersection has size k−1.

name: Codes and designs in Johnson graphs
description: Constant-weight codes and combinatorial designs correspond to cliques, cocliques, and perfect codes in Johnson graphs, with bounds derived from the Johnson scheme spectrum.

name: Maximal subgroups of finite simple groups
description: The classification and structural description of the maximal subgroups of the finite simple groups, organized via the O'Nan–Scott and Aschbacher reduction theorems.

name: O'Nan–Scott theorem
description: Every finite primitive permutation group falls into one of a small number of structural types (affine, almost simple, product action, diagonal, twisted wreath) determined by its socle.

name: Fair partition / Nandakumar–Ramana-Rao problem
description: The problem of partitioning a convex body in the plane into n convex pieces of equal area and equal perimeter.

name: Equivariant topology test-map method
description: A method that encodes a combinatorial problem as the search for a zero of a continuous equivariant map, then derives existence or nonexistence from equivariant topological invariants such as the Borsuk–Ulam property.

name: Hypergraph Turán problem
description: The problem of determining the maximum number of edges in an n-vertex r-uniform hypergraph containing no copy of a fixed forbidden r-uniform hypergraph.

name: Hypergraph Turán in the ℓ₂-norm
description: Results bounding the codegree-squared (ℓ₂-norm) extremal function of forbidden hypergraphs, a refinement of the hypergraph Turán problem measuring the second moment of the codegree sequence.

name: Circuit imbalance measure
description: The maximum absolute ratio of nonzero entries appearing in the support-minimal vectors (circuits) of the kernel of a matrix, a condition-number-like measure of a linear program.

name: Circuit imbalance and LP complexity
description: Linear programs can be solved in a number of arithmetic operations depending only on the dimension and the logarithm of the circuit imbalance measure of the constraint matrix, yielding strongly-polynomial bounds for well-conditioned classes.

name: Erdős–Ko–Rado theorem
description: For n ≥ 2k, the largest intersecting family of k-element subsets of an n-set has size C(n−1, k−1), attained by all k-sets through a fixed element.

name: Junta method for intersection problems
function_signature: (Large intersecting/forbidden-configuration family) → (Approximation by a junta + stability)
description: A technique showing that an extremal or near-extremal family in an intersection problem is essentially determined by a bounded number of coordinates (a junta), enabling exact and stability results.

name: Finite geometry constructions for extremal graphs
description: A method that builds dense graphs free of a fixed bipartite subgraph from incidence structures of finite projective planes, generalized polygons, and polarities.

name: Erdős–Rényi C₄-free polarity graph
description: The C₄-free graph on the points of a projective plane PG(2,q) in which two points are adjacent when one lies on the polar line of the other, attaining the Kővári–Sós–Turán bound ex(n;C₄)∼½n^{3/2}.

name: Rainbow subgraph / transversal
description: In an edge-colored graph or a collection of graphs, a subgraph all of whose edges have distinct colors, equivalently a transversal selecting one edge per color class.

name: Aharoni–Berger rainbow matching results
description: Results and conjectures asserting that n matchings of size n in a bipartite multigraph have a rainbow matching using one edge from each, generalizing Latin-square transversal problems.

name: Explicit bounds for graph minors
description: Quantitative bounds making the qualitative Robertson–Seymour structure theory effective, such as the polynomial grid-minor theorem relating treewidth to the largest grid minor.

name: Tropical geometry (combinatorial)
description: The geometry over the min-plus (tropical) semiring in which algebraic varieties degenerate to piecewise-linear polyhedral complexes, providing a combinatorial shadow of algebraic geometry.

name: Matroid Chow ring intersection theory
description: A method that proves combinatorial inequalities by computing degrees of products of divisor classes in the Chow ring of a matroid and invoking the Hodge–Riemann relations.

name: Erdős covering system
description: A finite collection of congruences x ≡ aᵢ (mod mᵢ) with distinct moduli whose union covers every integer.

name: Minimum modulus problem (Hough's theorem)
description: There is an absolute constant bounding the smallest modulus of any covering system with distinct moduli, so the minimum modulus cannot be arbitrarily large.

name: Cluster expansion
function_signature: (Partition function of a polymer model) → (Convergent power series for log Z)
description: A technique expressing the logarithm of a polymer-model partition function as an absolutely convergent series over connected clusters of polymers.

name: Polymer model
description: A statistical-mechanics abstraction whose partition function sums weighted collections of pairwise-compatible polymers, used to encode combinatorial counting and Gibbs-measure problems.

name: Kotecký–Preiss criterion
description: A sufficient condition on polymer weights guaranteeing absolute convergence of the cluster expansion of the corresponding polymer-model partition function.

name: Sublinear expander
description: A graph in which every not-too-large vertex subset expands by a factor that decays only polylogarithmically in its size, a weak expansion notion satisfied by all graphs of given average degree after passing to a subgraph.

name: Komlós–Szemerédi sublinear expander theorem
description: Every graph contains a subgraph of comparable average degree that is a sublinear expander, providing a universal expansion structure inside dense-enough graphs.

name: Sublinear-expander embedding method
function_signature: (Graph of given average degree) → (Embedded sparse subdivision / minor)
description: A technique using the short typical distances and robust connectivity of a sublinear expander to embed subdivisions, minors, and other sparse structures.

name: Transversal in a Latin square
description: A set of n cells in an n×n Latin square, one in each row and one in each column, whose entries are all distinct.

name: Ryser–Brualdi–Stein conjecture
description: The conjecture that every n×n Latin square has a partial transversal of size n−1, and a full transversal whenever n is odd.

name: Montgomery's transversal theorem
description: Every sufficiently large n×n Latin square contains a full transversal, asymptotically resolving the existence part of the Ryser–Brualdi–Stein conjecture.

name: Transshipment / flows over time
description: A network-flow model in which flow on each arc incurs a transit time, and supplies and demands at multiple sources and sinks must be routed within a given time horizon.

name: Quickest transshipment theorem (Hoppe–Tardos)
description: The quickest transshipment problem of routing given multi-terminal supplies and demands through a network with transit times in minimum total time is solvable in strongly polynomial time.

name: Oriented trees and paths in digraphs
description: The study of when a digraph or tournament of given size or minimum out-degree must contain a prescribed oriented tree or oriented path as a subdigraph.

name: Sumner's conjecture
description: The conjecture that every tournament on 2n−2 vertices contains every oriented tree on n vertices as a spanning subdigraph.

name: Gallai–Roy and Burr–Erdős directed-path results
description: The Gallai–Roy theorem that every orientation of a graph with chromatic number k contains a directed path on k vertices, together with related Burr–Erdős bounds on long directed paths.

name: Sidorenko's conjecture
description: The conjecture that for every bipartite graph H, the homomorphism density of H in any graphon W is at least the edge density of W raised to the number of edges of H.
